drivers/gpu/drm/amd/display/amdgpu_dm/am.specific_evidence: Physical AMD/Intel graphics driver changes. The recorded common x86 configuration disables DRM_AMDGPU, DRM_I915 and DRM_XE, while the virtual-device module set explicitly supplies virtio-gpu, goldfish display transport and vkms. A host GPU used to accelerate the emulator is not an AMD/Intel PCI display device assigned to this SDK guest. Keep native LTS driver code; generic DRM APIs are separate decisions.

drivers/firmware/arm_ffa/driver.c.specific_evidence: ARM SMMU/GIC/firmware implementation. Local Kconfig constrains these to ARM/ARM64 or explicit compile-test, and the SDK is the ordinary x86_64 product. Exclude ACK ARM/protected-host additions while retaining pinned LTS. Generic IOMMU/IRQ interfaces and hooks are reviewed and ported separately.

decisions.method: Every residual path belongs to the reviewed opt-in Intel pKVM protected-host backend, another architecture, historical KMI, or a separately reviewed physical-device path. The supplied SDK kernel command-line contract and ACK zero-initialized enable_pkvm/early-parameter gate establish the excluded protected-host mode. Retain exact LTS blobs. Shared KVM/MM/IOMMU and guest-ABI paths are not admitted by this completion. See SECURITY.md: Intel pKVM host-only subset and evidence/generic-source-review.json. This does not claim broader AVF runtime compatibility. Merge resolutions remain separately indexed.

arch/x86/kvm/vmx/pkvm_init.c.specific_evidence: This path implements the Intel pKVM protected-host backend, not ordinary upstream KVM. In pinned ACK arch/x86/kvm/pkvm.c, enable_pkvm is a zero-initialized bool; vmx/pkvm_init.c sets it only via early kvm-intel.pkvm parsing and exits before hypervisor setup when false. The supplied goldfish board/kernel/x86_64.mk explicitly installs x86_64_cmdline.txt, whose complete contents are 8250.nr_uarts=1 clocksource=pit. This current SDK boot contract does not request the protected-host mode. Omit this backend for the current target and retain exact LTS state. Ordinary Intel/AMD KVM stays enabled. This does not assert that all AVF userspace is absent, that nested virtualization cannot exist, or that future protected-VM requirements are resolved; the decision is limited to the supplied ordinary SDK boot configuration.

The supplied goldfish board/kernel/x86_64.mk explicitly installs x86_64_cmdline.txt, whose complete contents are 8250.nr_uarts=1 clocksource=pit. This does not assert that all AVF userspace is absent, that nested virtualization cannot exist, or that future protected-VM requirements are resolved; the decision is limited to the supplied ordinary SDK boot configuration.

GrapheneOS does contain Gunyah/GenieZone userspace support: virtmgr/crosvm.rs add_gunyah_specific_arg is gated by hypervisor_props::is_gunyah, which checks the hypervisor version property. Thus this is an architecture/backend selection decision, not a claim of absent Android consumers or absent virtualization generally. Ordinary KVM and shared MM/IOMMU APIs are reviewed separately.

The supplied goldfish board/kernel/x86_64.mk explicitly installs x86_64_cmdline.txt, whose complete contents are 8250.nr_uarts=1 clocksource=pit. This current SDK boot contract does not request the protected-host mode. Omit this backend for the current target and retain exact LTS state. Ordinary Intel/AMD KVM stays enabled. This does not assert that all AVF userspace is absent, that nested virtualization cannot exist, or that future protected-VM requirements are resolved; the decision is limited to the supplied ordinary SDK boot configuration.

The supplied goldfish board/kernel/x86_64.mk explicitly installs x86_64_cmdline.txt, whose complete contents are 8250.nr_uarts=1 clocksource=pit. This current SDK boot contract does not request the protected-host mode. Omit this backend for the current target and retain exact LTS state. Ordinary Intel/AMD KVM stays enabled. This does not assert that all AVF userspace is absent, that nested virtualization cannot exist, or that future protected-VM requirements are resolved; the decision is limited to the supplied ordinary SDK boot configuration.

The supplied goldfish board/kernel/x86_64.mk explicitly installs x86_64_cmdline.txt, whose complete contents are 8250.nr_uarts=1 clocksource=pit. This current SDK boot contract does not request the protected-host mode. Omit this backend for the current target and retain exact LTS state. Ordinary Intel/AMD KVM stays enabled. This does not assert that all AVF userspace is absent, that nested virtualization cannot exist, or that future protected-VM requirements are resolved; the decision is limited to the supplied ordinary SDK boot configuration.

drivers/dma-buf/dma-buf.c.specific_evidence: Full LTS and normalized-ACK residuals reviewed. Retain accounting for per-process DMA-buf RSS/PSS and high-water marks: pinned GrapheneOS lmkd.cpp reads dmabuf_pss for victim sizing, and libmeminfo has procfs API tests (read, not executed). State uses refcounts and locks, counts actual child FDs/VMAs, shares only when both MM/files are shared, and intentionally leaves partial sharing/kernel threads unaccounted. Preallocation avoids sleeping under the accounting spinlock; 54fdb0c6e4bd trims unused records after fork and failed preallocation so duplicate FDs/VMAs cannot leave an unbounded per-CPU cache. Keep Android buffer iteration, naming, partial CPU-access and flags APIs plus release hook; 90d9af708fea guards NULL partial-end access and supplies zero default flags. Native LTS mapping bounds, reservation/fence waits, poll, sync-file ioctls and release behavior remain. Accounting failures on mmap log and preserve successful mapping; fork/exec allocations can fail with ENOMEM. Cross-file VMA/fd/fork lifecycle paths retain separate candidate reviews. No runtime correctness or OOM-policy test claim. Incremental review a7db20b7e4ce: count duplicate references without allocation; after a missing new record, keep tracking/draining existing records but prohibit new records and return EIO from RSS/PSS/HWM interfaces. This avoids an untracked close subtracting a later unrelated attribution. Details and compatibility/security limitations are in evidence/dmabuf-accounting-local-review.json and SECURITY.md. No native LTS I/O, fence or file lifetime path is replaced.

drivers/dma-buf/heaps/system_heap.c.specific_evidence: Full LTS delta reviewed. Preserve cached and system-uncached heaps: pinned GrapheneOS BufferAllocator::AllocSystem selects the latter for no-CPU-access requests and explicitly falls back to system when absent; actual virtual-device rules build this module. Keep write-combined user/kernel mappings, zeroed pages, matching DMA attributes, and refuse uncached SWIOTLB mappings that cannot maintain the intended coherence contract. df0acacabb95 checks every SG entry instead of repeatedly checking the first, propagates initial map failure and releases the exported buffer without invalid unmap, validates DMA setup and release-publishes the allocator. If optional uncached registration fails after cached publication, retain cached service and successful module initialization so callbacks cannot point into freed failed-init module text. Mask-setup failure drops the uncached registration reference; existing open references may delay disappearance and see EBUSY. On x86 PAGE_SHIFT=12 allocation orders remain the LTS 8/4/0 values. No runtime allocation, cache-coherence, IOMMU/SWIOTLB or fault-injection validation.

drivers/dma-buf/dma-buf.c.specific_evidence: Full LTS and normalized-ACK residuals reviewed. Retain accounting for per-process DMA-buf RSS/PSS and high-water marks: pinned GrapheneOS lmkd.cpp reads dmabuf_pss for victim sizing, and libmeminfo has procfs API tests (read, not executed). State uses refcounts and locks, counts actual child FDs/VMAs, shares only when both MM/files are shared, and intentionally leaves partial sharing/kernel threads unaccounted. Preallocation avoids sleeping under the accounting spinlock; 54fdb0c6e4bd trims unused records after fork and failed preallocation so duplicate FDs/VMAs cannot leave an unbounded per-CPU cache. Keep Android buffer iteration, naming, partial CPU-access and flags APIs plus release hook; 90d9af708fea guards NULL partial-end access and supplies zero default flags. Native LTS mapping bounds, reservation/fence waits, poll, sync-file ioctls and release behavior remain. Accounting failures on mmap log and preserve successful mapping; fork/exec allocations can fail with ENOMEM. Cross-file VMA/fd/fork lifecycle paths retain separate candidate reviews. No runtime correctness or OOM-policy test claim. Incremental review a7db20b7e4ce: count duplicate references without allocation; after a missing new record, keep tracking/draining existing records but prohibit new records and return EIO from RSS/PSS/HWM interfaces. This avoids an untracked close subtracting a later unrelated attribution. Details and compatibility/security limitations are in evidence/dmabuf-accounting-local-review.json and SECURITY.md. No native LTS I/O, fence or file lifetime path is replaced.

drivers/dma-buf/heaps/system_heap.c.specific_evidence: Full LTS delta reviewed. Preserve cached and system-uncached heaps: pinned GrapheneOS BufferAllocator::AllocSystem selects the latter for no-CPU-access requests and explicitly falls back to system when absent; actual virtual-device rules build this module. Keep write-combined user/kernel mappings, zeroed pages, matching DMA attributes, and refuse uncached SWIOTLB mappings that cannot maintain the intended coherence contract. df0acacabb95 checks every SG entry instead of repeatedly checking the first, propagates initial map failure and releases the exported buffer without invalid unmap, validates DMA setup and release-publishes the allocator. Mask-setup failure drops the uncached registration reference; existing open references may delay disappearance and see EBUSY. On x86 PAGE_SHIFT=12 allocation orders remain the LTS 8/4/0 values. No runtime allocation, cache-coherence, IOMMU/SWIOTLB or fault-injection validation.

Retain accounting for per-process DMA-buf RSS/PSS and high-water marks: pinned GrapheneOS lmkd.cpp reads dmabuf_pss for victim sizing, and libmeminfo has procfs API tests (read, not executed). State uses refcounts and locks, counts actual child FDs/VMAs, shares only when both MM/files are shared, and intentionally leaves partial sharing/kernel threads unaccounted. Preallocation avoids sleeping under the accounting spinlock; 54fdb0c6e4bd trims unused records after fork and failed preallocation so duplicate FDs/VMAs cannot leave an unbounded per-CPU cache. Keep Android buffer iteration, naming, partial CPU-access and flags APIs plus release hook; 90d9af708fea guards NULL partial-end access and supplies zero default flags. Native LTS mapping bounds, reservation/fence waits, poll, sync-file ioctls and release behavior remain. Accounting failures on mmap log and preserve successful mapping; fork/exec allocations can fail with ENOMEM. Cross-file VMA/fd/fork lifecycle paths retain separate candidate reviews. No runtime correctness or OOM-policy test claim. Incremental review a7db20b7e4ce: count duplicate references without allocation; after a missing new record, keep tracking/draining existing records but prohibit new records and return EIO from RSS/PSS/HWM interfaces. This avoids an untracked close subtracting a later unrelated attribution. Details and compatibility/security limitations are in evidence/dmabuf-accounting-local-review.json and SECURITY.md. No native LTS I/O, fence or file lifetime path is replaced.

drivers/misc/uid_sys_stats.c.specific_evidence: Reviewed entire added implementation and full normalized-ACK delta. Retain per-UID CPU/IO snapshots and foreground/background controls: pinned KernelCpuUidTimeReader and StoragedUidIoStatsReader consume these exact proc formats; system_server has SELinux write rules and genfs labels. Host checks execute the actual function with a hash shim under ASan/UBSan, including UINT_MAX/full-range and malformed bounds. UID data/worker locking and copied exit statistics avoid task-pointer lifetime dependence; failed allocation or a deferred update whose UID entry was removed/missing can lose statistics. Counters are observational, not security/resource limits; namespace attribution and concurrent snapshots are not runtime-certified. Final ACK reverted fsync syscall tracking, leaving those format columns zero. Runtime OEM fields have actual hook consumers; no KMI padding retained.

Retain GPL file_close_fd export and Android close_fd source namespace. Remaining file equals normalized ACK; no historical KMI layout retained. Positive lmkd dmabuf PSS/RSS and libmeminfo proc consumers are documented in SECURITY.md.

Keep cpufreq time allocation/init/free, actual vendor/OEM runtime data initialization, task/MM hooks and source exports. Proxy scheduling fields/locks/lists are initialized for the retained implementation; its scheduling algorithms are assessed separately. Integrity-hook failure uses bad_fork_core_free, preserving both locks and scheduler cleanup. Preserve native LTS early BPF initialization, CLONE_VM futex-hash sharing including vfork, PF_BLOCK_TS clearing and namespace API. Accounting OOM can fail fork; no runtime fork/race certification. 85c809fbcecd only adds task vendor allocation setup before cache creation; the previously reviewed fork/teardown code is otherwise byte-preserved. Append aligned vendor bytes after native architecture allocation and compute the native usercopy whitelist first. Default zero-request allocation is unchanged; offset/size become read-only after init. See evidence/task-vendor-storage-review.json and focused host checks. Scoped follow-up 275786041b29: the only fork change since checkpoint 82cebd796d84 removes INIT_LIST_HEAD(&p->migration_node), matching removal of an obsolete field positively replaced by se.group_node in 15dd0824de4d. Complete remaining file is byte-identical, so prior allocation, hooks, accounting, security and teardown findings are unchanged. See evidence/proxy-donor-chain-review.json. Scoped follow-up f6617750f7d3: the sole fork change since 5af9f5bdb352 initializes copied wake_q_count to zero alongside wake_q.next. fs/file.c.specific_evidence: Reviewed all LTS and normalized-ACK differences and complete do_dup2/close/fd-install paths with DMA accounting implementation. Retain accounting before fd publication, unaccount before last file release, files_struct ownership, and removal of task accounting on partial sharing. do_dup2 holds a file reference while dropping file_lock for preallocation; on relock it re-reads the table and preserves native reserved-slot EBUSY/nospec checks. Rollback unaccounts and drops the added file reference; replaced files are unaccounted before close. Allocation failure in fd_install is best effort: it logs and installs the descriptor, so counters can undercount under OOM and are not resource limits. Retain GPL file_close_fd export and Android close_fd source namespace. Remaining file equals normalized ACK; no historical KMI layout retained. Positive lmkd dmabuf PSS/RSS and libmeminfo proc consumers are documented in SECURITY.md.

Callbacks run under existing local/spin locks where applicable, must not sleep, and are trusted code; entry/flag mutations must honor allocator accounting contracts. Exact optional SDK callback use is unresolved and conservatively retained. c0cbe76ff03a translates Android Toybox/mmd/fs_mgr emulated swap formats without cached-header mutation, preserving native validation and capacity bounds, and reserves the entire header in map and clusters. d7f2fd2bd53e stores activation classification in SWP_SOLIDSTATE so a changed/unregistered hibernation callback cannot unbalance nr_rotate_swap on swapoff; both callback sites remain. Native LTS atomic_long counter mask, reclaim cond_resched, rate-limited corrupt-entry diagnostics, encrypted-file rejection, percpu-reference shutdown and error unwinds remain. Host extracted-code checks cover header/map/cluster paths and hook classification; no real swap, extent, concurrency or runtime tests. Dual-signature ambiguity and the unchanged native bad-table bound are documented in SECURITY.md.

Restricted allocation callbacks must honor native order/context and ordinary callbacks must not sleep under page-table/XArray locks or retain unowned pointers. The lock-drop callbacks explicitly receive fpin; a dropped fault lock means the VMA is unavailable. 8d75f9fa7f08 passes NULL after that drop, pins the unlocked mapped-folio callback, and snapshots index before write_end can free the folio. 15bccdfefe6d skips prefetch for all-padding VMAs and snapshots data bounds before unlock, preventing unsigned executable-window underflow; host extracted checks cover old-source failures. Cleancache uses b1ae0b82acce large-folio invalidation to avoid stale base-page cache data. Keep native xas_nomem original-order reset, mapped-folio dropbehind protection and file_owner_or_capable cachestat authorization. Cachestat units follow Android emulation while native permission checks remain. 7f9fdddd5bf8 fixes EOF snapshot/ref cleanup; shared EOF-tail semantics remain specifically provisional under b3c77090341c and are not certified by this path review. Large-folio mapping granularity is byte-identical to both inputs as separately recorded. This review covers generic Android source/configuration compatibility, not historical module binary layout. Successful workflow and focused host checks do not verify real page faults, concurrency or runtime SDK behavior.

Every path has this scoped review, a still-valid prior final witness, identity or explicit architecture/KMI exclusion. Shared EOF-tail, DMA-buf OOM accounting, memsize reporting and rmap/UFFD concurrency remain separate reviews; no runtime compatibility claim.

include/linux/mm.h.specific_evidence: Full LTS/normalized-ACK header deltas reviewed against implementations. Keep page-size padding flag fixup and boot-time ASLR bounds as ro_after_init, page-pinner put observation, generic longterm-pin customization and reviewed reclaim/allocator source declarations. VM_NO_REMAP_FILE_PAGES has a positive Rust wrapfd consumer preventing remap_file_pages from restoring forbidden write capability. Native LTS VM_MAYBE_GUARD, atomic-set allowed-mask, sticky merge and fork copying protections stay intact; obsolete ACK huge-page declarations and old MM CID exit name do not override LTS. The put callback runs before the caller frees a last-reference page; longterm-pinnable override is trusted module policy requiring DMA/migration safety. Native seal/guard protection is not bypassed by padding fixup. Shared EOF-tail and DMA-buf lifecycle candidates remain explicitly excluded from this scope.

mm/mlock.c.specific_evidence: Full LTS delta is page-size header integration and emulated alignment for mlock/munlock entry ranges. Preserve RLIMIT_MEMLOCK and locked_vm accounting in actual native page units, CAP_IPC_LOCK checks, writer locking, zero/wrapped-range validation and native population/error behavior. Caller ranges are aligned before the stronger internal assertions. Keep newer LTS zone_stat_mod_folio accounting and vma_modify_flags pointer update so merged sticky guard flags are retained. Bionic/Android receive the configured emulated page-size ABI; this does not enlarge locking authority or import historical KMI layouts. Native 4 KiB behavior is unchanged; no runtime locking test.

mm/mprotect.c.specific_evidence: Full LTS delta changes only include dependencies, start-alignment validation and length rounding to the emulated page size. Preserve native pkey validation, VM_MAY access limits, map_deny_write_exec, architecture checks, security_file_mprotect, vm_ops callbacks and TLB/lock sequencing. Keep LTS vma_modify_flags pointer API so updated sticky flags survive merging. Padding handling stays in separately reviewed common VMA helpers. Positive page_shift=14 requires the corresponding syscall page granularity; native mode is unchanged. Diagnostic rate limiting is in c476769367dd. No runtime protection test claimed.

include/linux/mmzone.h.specific_evidence: Full header delta reviewed with allocator, lruvec and node initialization. Retain source CMA migration type/list changes, generic vendor/OEM storage and source isolation declarations; omit historical binary layout promises. MIGRATE_FALLBACKS separates ordinary fallback/merge types from CMA, enum limits still cover all native types and the bitmap. 38e13dcb4814 adds a third high-order PCP list only for CMA/THP; all initialization/draining iterates NR_PCP_LISTS and pindex_to_order handles each high-order list. lruvec_init zeroes the entire structure; per-node memcg allocations use __GFP_ZERO and mm/numa.c alloc_node_data explicitly clears sizeof(pg_data_t), so new fields initialize with rebuilt structure sizes. The isolation APIs require caller locks and their existing bool/count return contracts. No historical KMI layout retention or future-platform controller added.

mm/migrate.c.specific_evidence: Full LTS/normalized-ACK deltas and complete batch cleanup reviewed. Keep native migration/isolation exports for rebuilt vendor modules plus statistics, policy and bypass hooks. Entry-wait start runs while the page-table lock still stabilizes the entry; end only uses copied scalar time/zone. Folio-state hooks run with native owned folios. Split bypass returns EBUSY through ordinary failure handling. Batch-break occurs after paired source/destination lists are populated and still performs TLB flush, move retries and undo; callbacks must supply a valid remaining count and preserve list ownership. ab9389a3d802 defaults the break count to zero before each callback. Migration batch size remains trusted policy and must be positive. A remove-migration-PTE bypass takes responsibility for the skipped operation, not a permission granted to userspace. Retain newer LTS enum ttu_flags/TTU_RMAP_LOCKED/TTU_USE_SHARED_ZEROPAGE semantics, PMD migration predicate and cond_resched_tasks_rcu_qs. Source selection only; no runtime migration or race test.

mm/page_alloc.c.specific_evidence: Full LTS and normalized ACK deltas, allocation/free/PCP/drain/compaction/reclaim/contiguous callers reviewed. Retain generic Android allocation, watermarks, diagnostic and pool policy hooks, __GFP_CMA restricted redirect, CMA PCP lists, validated pcp_thp_order boot parameter and rebuilt module APIs. 38e13dcb4814 separates high-order CMA lists, preserves the original fallback pointer and excludes CMA from ordinary mobility-group relabeling. Host extracted selection tests cover CMA/THP configurations, all accepted high orders and old failures. 72565355d3de resets zone/retry policy, initializes reclaim progress and honors returned pages. Callbacks remain trusted: zone/order/batch changes must remain in bounds, returned pages must meet frozen/refcount/zeroing/memcg contracts, free/list bypasses take responsibility for skipped validation, initialization and accounting, and source isolation helpers require the native zone/LRU locking. __GFP_NORETRY contiguous requests use bounded async migration while preserving the native GFP validation and cleanup. prep/free_hpage_order preserve explicit order for noncompound pages; prep_compound_page remains separate. Native LTS capture-control lifetime, barriers, direct-compaction/reclaim order promotion, reclaim lockdep and UP-NMI deferred free remain. Page-pinner/free and memsize bookkeeping do not replace allocation checks; optional memsize accuracy remains separate and its multi-file candidates are not finalized here. Actual SDK enables CMA/GCMA with no configured fixed pool, so exact runtime pool use remains unconfirmed and conservatively retained. No running allocator/CMA concurrency test. Scoped follow-up 8e8cbee1ce28 removes only report-only memsize accounting from free_reserved_area, restoring that function to native LTS. All allocator, CMA PCP and callback fixes remain. Memsize selection is now final for this target as documented in SECURITY.md; the older note about pending report accuracy is superseded only for this omitted report. Native free/page poisoning and statistics are unchanged.

mm/vmscan.c.specific_evidence: Full LTS/normalized-ACK deltas and reclaim loops, MM walk lifetime, mapping removal, asynchronous list/ref ownership and module exports reviewed. Preserve generic Android scan/folio/memcg/slab/PSI policy hooks with native defaults. 72565355d3de scopes folio and memcg decisions to each iteration and applies the native no-progress stop to vendor MGLRU reclaim; 429 host extracted scan/protection/rotation cases pass. In __remove_mapping the keep callback runs after folio_ref_freeze and must restore the supplied reference count before keeping it; writeback/eviction bypasses must assume skipped list/reference obligations. MADV_PAGEOUT private begin/list/end callbacks must move/consume remaining folios and preserve context lifetime; default NULL private uses native putback. Hooks run under their existing locks/RCU and may intentionally override reclaim protections/PSI policy as trusted kernel code, not userspace authority. No actual pressure, fault, concurrent teardown or Android runtime test.

mm/vmscan.c.specific_evidence: Full LTS/normalized-ACK deltas and reclaim loops, MM walk lifetime, mapping removal, asynchronous list/ref ownership and module exports reviewed. drivers/block/zram/zram_drv.c.specific_evidence: Complete LTS-to-port and normalized-ACK deltas read, with full compressed writeback, prefetch, slot-free/replacement, completion, sysfs and I/O ownership paths. Retain compressed batched writeback and prefetch backing-copy cache: local mmd_setup.rs enables compressed_writeback, service.rs gates per-process operations on it, and per_process_ioctls.rs uses the range/prefetch/version ABI. Free request resources before completing. Original raw compressed page tail zeroing remains, preserving confidentiality on full-page backing writes. Native page/slot references and swap-level ownership protect normal fault reads; concurrent arbitrary raw-device overwrite is not promised an atomic snapshot. Slot metadata becomes u32 seconds/flags, retaining the big-endian lock-bit correction without claiming subsecond idle telemetry. Prefetch is best effort: deferred I/O/population failures do not report all missed hints to userspace. Process budget counts matching swap entries, not guaranteed successful writes; result bytes count completed physical writes and omit cache reuse. 35b41a30b529 uses native compat_ptr dispatch for identical ioctl layouts in the already-enabled IA32 configuration, preserving checks. 21 extracted-function error/cleanup cases and deterministic last-notifier interleaving checks pass with old-source controls; no actual I/O or memory-pressure race run.

Actual driver functions pass 21 host-shim cases covering permission/init/busy/allocation/scan/write errors, output counts and cleanup; old controls reproduce failures. No live task page walk, swapoff or authorization test.

Retain version 1, legacy writeback, bounded range writeback and process prefetch, guarded by device access plus global capable(CAP_SYS_NICE) for process operations. This intentionally uses get_task_mm rather than ptrace mm_access: current range API returns next_addr and byte counts, so old commit 4191645fc555 claim that no address metadata is exposed does not apply to the final ABI. Accept that privileged daemon metadata/performance authority for Android compatibility; do not claim unprivileged isolation from a SYS_NICE holder with device access. Local mmd.te permits only mmd for current ioctls and denies legacy to every domain. Native file owner/write check limits shared file pageout; pidfd/task/mm refs, mmap lock, PTE snapshot lock, swap device reference/type/non-swap and bounds checks remain. PTE snapshot can become stale before marking a slot, so selection is approximate; global post-processing exclusion and slot flags prevent old data replacing a newly written-back generation. 8e348642e1f0 initializes next_addr/written_bytes before all failures, including the legacy stack temporary; SDK stack initialization already mitigates uninitialized automatic data, and no ABI sizes or command values change. Actual driver functions pass 21 host-shim cases covering permission/init/busy/allocation/scan/write errors, output counts and cleanup; old controls reproduce failures. No live task page walk, swapoff or authorization test.
